fieldNotes.siteIdentification: The Crowley-served container terminal in the Manzanillo / Coco Solo Sur area of Colon, Panama is Manzanillo International Terminal (MIT), operated by SSA Marine. Crowley maintains its Panama liner-terminal office at Puerto de Manzanillo, Edificio C (Edificio de Navieras), Colon, and runs twice-weekly liner service to/from Colon out of MIT, using the terminal plus shared bonded/non-bonded warehouse space as its Atlantic hub. Confirmed against Crowley Panama pages, MIT/SSA Marine pages, latitude.to (9.357N -79.899W cited; corrected by imagery to the terminal centroid), and the GA Tech / Log Cluster (LCA) Panama port assessment. Center locked by satellite to ~9.3635N, -79.8835W (Manzanillo Bay peninsula, Coco Solo Sur).
fieldNotes.yardSpots: trailerParkingCapacity (~9,000) is a CONTAINER / CHASSIS GROUND-SLOT estimate, not OTR trailer stalls. MIT publishes 37 hectares (~91 acres) of paved container yard with automatic stacking cranes (ASCs), RTGs, top-/side-picks and 3.5M TEU annual capacity. z16-z20 satellite shows very dense multi-row container ground slots under RTG/ASC straddle rows across the peninsula, plus a large RoRo vehicle staging area on the east. The ~9,000 figure is a coarse ground-slot order-of-magnitude for a 37 ha high-density stacking yard, flagged uncertain. dropArea band 50+.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Marine container terminal, so classic OTR dock doors are near-zero. The attached/adjacent warehouse buildings on the east side carry the loading doors: z17 satellite plus a 2022-10 Street View (pano IL3eQ...) show large roll-up loading shutters on a warehouse face. dockDoorCount ~8 (0-10 band) reflects only the warehouse loading doors visible/inferred, low confidence at this resolution.
fieldNotes.attachedWarehouse: A row of large warehouse buildings (purple/gray/blue roofs) sits on the landward east side at ~9.369N, -79.876W (z17). Crowley provides consolidation/deconsolidation, cross-dock, re-label/re-pack, pick-and-pack and bonded/non-bonded storage at its Colon hub; these warehouses are the attached cross-dock/transit-shed space. Counted in buildingCount and dockDoorCount.
fieldNotes.truckGate: truckGate=true (high confidence). Web sources (GA Tech Panama logistics portal / LCA assessment) state MIT has 3 entrance lanes and 3 exit lanes at the main truck gate, plus a separate intermodal rail ramp with 2 in / 2 out lanes. MIT is ISPS compliant with perimeter fencing, gates and CCTV. Street View (pano h6g9FF..., 2023-03) on the landside approach road looks west into the secured terminal past channelizing jersey barriers toward the gantry cranes. entryLanes=3, exitLanes=3.
fieldNotes.guardShack: guardShack=true (inferred high confidence). An ISPS-compliant major transshipment terminal with a 3+3-lane gate operates staffed security/guard booths at the gate complex; not individually resolved in the available imagery (Google car coverage stops at the public road outside the secured estate) but standard and corroborated by the ISPS / CCTV / controlled-access references.
fieldNotes.entryExit: entryExitSeparate=true: the gate has distinct entrance-lane and exit-lane groups (3 in, 3 out) per published terminal specs.
fieldNotes.multiStep: multiStep=true: a major automated container gate is a multi-stage process (gate-in / OCR / TOS check, then yard), and a separate rail intermodal ramp with its own 2+2 lanes adds a second controlled checkpoint stage.
fieldNotes.scale: scale=true inferred: weighbridges are standard at a 3.5M TEU ISPS container terminal enforcing VGM/weight rules; not individually pinpointed in imagery, flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: fastLaneOpportunity=true: a 3+3-lane gate with wide aprons and channelized lanes has physical room for an express/bypass lane.
fieldNotes.railServed: railServed=true: z17 satellite at the NE boundary (9.3705N, -79.8745W) shows live rail tracks with container flat cars (Panama Canal Railway intermodal yard); MIT publishes a rail intermodal ramp with 2 entrance / 2 exit lanes.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Urban: the terminal sits inside the Colon metro / Colon Free Trade Zone industrial fabric, dense surrounding warehouses and the city of Colon immediately west.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Campus-scale: container quay + ASC/RTG stacking yard, RoRo vehicle yard, the east-side warehouse row, rail intermodal yard, and ancillary terminal/workshop buildings.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: ~140 acres is the secured-estate estimate from the traced perimeter (container yard 37 ha / ~91 ac paved plus warehouses, RoRo yard and rail ramp); approximate, flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.streetView: Google car Street View covers the public landside approach roads (2022-2023 panos) but not inside the secured terminal. Approach pano h6g9FF-lyCr9k9Tz1qRWyg @ 9.36393,-79.87804 looks west (heading 266) toward the gate/cranes; used for both perimeter and truckGate. A 2022-10 pano (IL3eQ4Ts6ggsF53oWhsH3w) shows warehouse roll-up loading doors on the east side.
